title: Edge energy fluctuation: A unified theory of friction scaling laws in twisted layered material interfaces
abstract: Interlayer twisting in van der Waals (vdW) layered materials generates moire superlattices, unlocking unique opportunities for engineering their electronic and mechanical functionalities. Here, building on two key insights - the invariance of the potential energy of complete moire tiles during sliding, and the symmetry-breaking effect induced by the slider edge - we propose the concept of edge energy fluctuation (EEF) and demonstrate that the EEF governs the sliding energy barrier of finite-sized sliders. Interestingly, we found that even at a fixed twist angle and sliding direction, significant frictional anisotropy emerges when the slider edge is cut along different directions, resulting in distinct friction scaling laws. Furthermore, we present a friction engineering paradigm for twisted layered material interfaces through the deliberate introduction of hierarchical edges, offering a promising route for friction control in superlubric devices.
summary: This work introduces the Edge Energy Fluctuation (EEF) theory to model friction in twisted vdW materials. It shows that the friction barrier is dictated by the specific geometry and orientation of the slider edge, leading to predictable friction anisotropy. This provides a powerful, tunable paradigm for designing superlubric devices.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified theory to explain the friction scaling laws observed at the interfaces of twisted van der Waals (vdW) layered materials, moving beyond assumptions of periodic boundary conditions.
main_result: The friction is governed by the Edge Energy Fluctuation (EEF), which reveals a strong dependence on the edge's orientation, leading to predictable friction anisotropy and offering a method for friction engineering.
method: The authors derive the sliding energy barrier by calculating an edge integral expression involving the moiré potential, analyzing how the edge geometry dictates the energy landscape.
model_or_system: The system is twisted vdW layered materials forming moiré superlattices, where the sliding motion is modeled by considering the energy contribution from the incomplete moiré tiles at the slider edge.
key_observables: Friction scaling laws ($F \propto A^m$), the sliding energy barrier ($\Delta G$ or $\Delta E$), and the degree of friction anisotropy based on edge orientation ($	heta$).
important_parameters: Twist angle, slider size (A or R), and the edge orientation ($	heta$) relative to the moiré lattice vectors.
main_assumptions: The energy barrier is dominated by the moiré edge, and the edge region can be approximated as a belt of finite width ($w$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the moiré edge and define the edge energy (EEF); one figure shows the potential energy landscape for circular sliders, and another demonstrates the friction anisotropy dependence on edge orientation.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the EEF concept, deriving the general edge energy integral, applying this to specific slider shapes (circular, straight), and finally establishing the implications for friction anisotropy and hierarchical edge engineering.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter friction, the concept of energy barriers governed by boundary conditions and symmetry breaking in quasi-periodic systems has parallels with understanding dissipation or decoherence in open quantum systems.
